To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have characterized for the first time, the gut microbial ecosystem of the long-lived rodent Heterocephalus Glaber (Naked Mole-Rat) and that we have highlighted peculiarities related to its specific living environment, which are shared with human populations considered as models of healthy gut microbiome, such as centenarians.

the gut microbial ecosystem of the long-lived rodent naked mole-rat, living in a subterranean environment, shares peculiarities with the microbiomes of humans considered as models of healthy aging, suggesting that the gut microbiome may play an important role in the biology of longevity.

the gut microbial ecosystem of a long-lived mammal, the naked mole-rats, shares some peculiarities with other mammalian species that are considered as a model for healthy aging and longevity, suggesting that a healthy gut microbiota may play a role in promoting a healthy aging.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the intestinal microbial ecosystem in the naked mole-rats, an animal model for healthy aging and longevity, in comparison with human gut microbiota.
the gut microbiome, a complex ecosystem that is present in the digestive system of all animals, including humans.

unraveling the microbial diversity of the gut of a mammal species with exceptional longevity and resistance to cancer and aging, and with comparing its microbial diversity with other mammalian gut microbiomes, including human ones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the naked mole-rats are not a model for the study of human aging.
the naked mole-rats have an intestinal microbial ecosystem which is similar to that of other mammals, and that it is characterized by a high degree of resilience and adaptability.

the naked mole rat gut microbial community is a unique example of a highly adaptive and resilient microbial community that can thrive under the most challenging environmental conditions, such as the subterranean life of the naked mole rat.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

naked mole-rat gut microbiota is characterized by an enrichment in bacteria able of anaerobic respiration on soil sulfate, which are also shared with human centenarians and the Hadza, suggesting that this trait is a hallmark of the healthy gut microbiota and of an efficient host-microbiota relationship.
naked mole-rat, humans and other animals share a common core of microbial species in their gut, but each of these species is present in different abundance.
the naked mole-rats' gut microbial ecosystem is characterized by the enrichment of bacterial taxa able to metabolize the specific diet and environment of this rodent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the long-lived naked-mole rat is a promising model to study the gut microbiome-host relationship in the context of healthy aging.
naked mole-rats, despite their extreme longevity and healthspan, are not an exception to the rule of a healthy gut microbial ecosystem.

, despite the extreme differences in the living environment and lifestyle between the naked mole-rats and humans, some of the gut microbial features that are associated with a healthy and homeostatic gut microbiota are also present in this rodent.
